parts.html: A 48 m² apartment where we handled the full cycle: the interior design project, custom furniture, turnkey renovation, and decorating. The project has been completed. The gallery shows the visualizations first, then photos of the finished apartment.

The 48 square meters hold a kitchen-living room with a dining area, a separate bedroom, a bathroom, and an entrance hall. To keep the rooms uncluttered, we moved storage into floor-to-ceiling built-in furniture. The palette is beige, light gray, white, and light wood, with brass and black metal as accents.

The kitchen runs in a single line along the window: light beige handleless base fronts, a wood-look countertop, and the sink by the window. The wall above the countertop is clad in large wood-pattern tiles. Between the kitchen and the sofa is a round dining table, with a pendant of frosted tubes on a branching frame above it. The floor in the shared area is light marble-look tile.

A glass partition in a slim frame, lit along its edge, separates the entrance hall from the living room. Light from the room reaches the front door, and the entrance doesn’t open straight into the living room. The entrance hall has a full-wall wardrobe with oak-look fronts. Shelving runs along the living room wall, with closed white sections alternating with open wooden shelves.

The bedroom has a light oak-look floor and, next to the headboard, a wooden panel with vertical slats and an LED strip along the edge. Brass loop lamps with white shades hang by the bed. The window has heavy curtains in the wall color and white sheers, with the curtain track recessed into the ceiling. A wardrobe with wooden fronts runs along one wall, and a TV hangs on the wall opposite the bed.

In the bathroom, the walls and floor are marble-look tile. The wall with the concealed frame for the wall-hung toilet is covered in wood-look panels up to the ceiling, leaving only the flush plate visible. There is a bathtub with a glass screen, a wall-hung vanity with drawers, and a mirror with perimeter lighting. We chose the curtains, cushions, and decor throughout the apartment — that was the decorating part of the job.
